title: Rice domestication in the Lower Yangtze (Shangshan culture)
summary: In the Lower Yangtze valley of Zhejiang, people of the Shangshan culture were using and processing wild rice by about 11,000 years ago. Rice with reduced seed shattering, a domestication trait, is documented at Huxi by 9,000–8,400 years ago. Scholars dispute exactly when rice became fully domesticated, and the process was gradual.

uncertainty.note: Years BP converted without a 1950 adjustment. Start follows the 2024 phytolith study; the earlier-start debate (pre-domestication from about 13,000 years ago) and the late end (full domestication later) are not included.

as_recorded.calendar: Years ago, phytolith and luminescence dating
as_recorded.value: about 11,000 years ago domesticated rice phytolith share rose rapidly

where.modern_name: Pujiang County, Jinhua, Zhejiang, China (Shangshan site)
where.historical_name: Upper Puyang River basin, Lower Yangtze region, Zhejiang; Neolithic, no polities

importance.justification: Rice, domesticated in this region, became a staple for much of humanity, and Shangshan is among the earliest known sites of rice use.

reviewer_note: Domestication timing is contested (wild, transitional or domesticated); the span here is a compromise of opened sources. The record id suggests c. 7450 BCE but opened sources support about 9000–6450 BCE, so the id and dates differ. Pujiang County centroid is used for the Shangshan site; exact site coordinates not opened.
